answer.summary: Donna recommends treating desired personal changes like product hypotheses: build on what is already working, take a tiny step, experiment, gather data, and use what you learn to adjust and scale gradually. When testing changes in yourself, consider head, heart, and hands—not just measurable results.

sections.heading: Start from what works, then test a small step
sections.content: Rather than forcing a sweeping change, notice what is already working and use it to identify a possibility you want to explore. Take one tiny step and run a small experiment to get data. Treat what you think is true—or what you want to do—as a hypothesis until you test it; then use what you learn to make informed decisions and try a bigger version gradually. Donna says this iterative approach applies to personal growth as well as products and businesses.

sections.heading: Check more than the numbers
sections.content: For experiments involving yourself, other people, teams, or companies, Donna suggests three filters: head (your thoughts about how it is going), heart (your emotional response), and hands (what you are doing). So evaluate the experience across these dimensions, rather than looking only at numerical outcomes.
